newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast Caistab's new boss takes over.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast Caistab's new boss takes over.

text.p: The newly appointed head of Ivory Coast's Caistab, Yves-Marie Koissy, has officially taken charge of the commodity marketing board and is expected to speed up donor-sponsored reforms.
Former Caistab chief Rene Amany stepped down officially on Wednesday after 17 years at the head of Ivory Coast's powerful commodity marketing monopoly, the Caistab told Reuters.
Koissy, who arrived from his job at the International Monetary Fund in Washington, is expected to push through market reforms to meet conditions for a $150 million World Bank loan.

Koissy, 42, studied economics and banking in Paris before moving to the Bank of France as a financial analyst and the IMF as an administrator. He has also been a World Bank advisor and an Ivorian bank credit manager.

Koissy is a technocrat seen as close to Ivorian president Henri Konan Bedie, who came to power after the death of veteran leader Felix Houphouet-Boigny in December 1993 and won elections in October last year.
Early reforms expected at the Caistab include revsion of a new automated produce auctioning system put in place in May to increase market efficiency and transparency.
Amany was dimissed without explanation on September 12. Koissy remained in Washington until Wednesday as an IMF economist and leaves again for Washington on Thursday until the end of the month.

Ivory Coast's 1996/97 cocoa marketing season was set in September to open on Ocober 15. Producer prices and other marketing rates have yet to be announced. --Matthew Bunce, Abidjan Newsroom +225 21 90 90 E-mail, WW.ABJ@REUTERS.COM
